purpose: Bring player and net scale closer to the game's base view and leave room around animated palm crowns.

variants.prompt:
Refine this gameplay concept, preserving its moonlit realistic 3D style, warm player lighting, dark cool beach, simple hotel silhouette, palette, wall architecture, and character identities. This is a precise layout correction, not a new scene.
The image currently makes the players and center net much too large for the game. Move the continuous straight collision-floor edge down to exactly 87% of frame height; below it retain only a shallow dark foreground plinth. Keep both straight wall faces at x=4% and x=96%, full height, with clearly illuminated inner edges meeting the floor.
Shrink both humans as complete anatomically consistent figures: the standing woman's entire height must be only 17% of image height, with her feet on y=87%, top of head around y=70%. Preserve her coral outfit and ready stance at x=72%. The jumping man must have the same anatomical scale as her, approximately 60% of his current size; keep him airborne at x=33%, body center around y=67%, full hands and feet inside the frame. Shrink the yellow/blue ball proportionately to about 3% image height and place it just beyond his raised hand. Keep warm skin and bright teal/coral clothing sharply visible against the dark quiet backdrop.
The thin central net pole must start at y=87% and stop at y=66%, only 21% of the image height, not the current giant tall pole. Retain a narrow edge-on mesh strip. Lower the two circular service buttons to around y=70%.
Reduce the size of each palm crown so every outer leaf tip is inside the background opening with some clear sky around it; crowns must not be clipped at the image border. Keep palms sparse, separately readable and suitable for gentle wind animation. Retain a broad simple ocean band behind the characters, with fewer bright tiny wave details and only broad reflection ribbons. Keep plant clusters behind the court near the sides, not overlapping floor, players or wall edges. No new objects, no text or HUD, no diagrams. The complete final image should read as a playable side-view arena with small realistic ragdoll tourists and crisp continuous floor and wall boundaries.
